text:
maria: Heads-up — got a customer report: a long-running chat (8h) hit a host OOM, node evicted. Suspect KV growth from reuse pointers not compacting.
jamal: any repro traces? which model & kernel?
maria: running gpt-medium-12b-quant, cudnn-fallback kernel for a stretch, sustained seq len ~6k. Attached logs show steady rv_alloc growth.
oliver: saw a similar pattern last month but that was a leak in the reuse window. Can you paste the memprof snippet?
maria: here —
```
KV_POOL_TOTAL: 24GB
KV_POOL_USED: 23.1GB -> 23.8GB (8h)
REUSE_POINTERS_ACTIVE: 1.2M -> 1.9M
EVICT_CYCLES: every 30s, reclaimed 10-30MB
PAGEING_RATE: 0.2/s
```
jamal: interesting — evict cycles running but reclaim low. Sounds like fragmentation + many small pinned fragments.
tessa: @jamal @maria is the background compaction job running? we had compaction disabled in the canary kernel switch last week.
maria: compaction was off on that host (flag: --kv-compaction=off) because of a perf experiment.
jamal: that explains it. Without compaction, reuse creates many small slabs and reclaim is inefficient. But we should still avoid full OOM. Proposed mitigations: 1) incremental-evict-throttle: increase aggressiveness when longctx detected, 2) soft-degrade route to short-context model variant, 3) enable emergency autoshrink for canary hosts.
oliver: +1. Also add a fast-path eviction that can coalesce adjacent small slabs at throttle time (cheap best-effort).
tessa: what about retries/fallback for in-flight requests? if evict blocks, we should surface a 503 or fallback to hosted.
jamal: yeah add a graceful-degrade policy: when host memory>90% for >5m, mark host read-only for longctx sessions, route new long contexts away, and for active long sessions we can inject a periodic KV trim that evicts oldest prefixes beyond N tokens.
maria: I sketched a short checklist:
- immediate: flip --kv-compaction back on for canary hosts (rollback experiment)
- short (1 day): deploy incremental-evict-throttle feature flag + metrics (evict_reclaimed_bytes, frag_ratio)
- medium (1 week): implement best-effort slab coalescer in eviction path
- fallback: route to short-context model and surface 503 with message to client

jamal: also add kernel selection guard: if kernel==cudnn-fallback and compaction==off and avg_seq_len>2k -> prefer alternate kernel that triggers compaction-friendly allocator. That will avoid mismatched kernel+allocator combos.
tessa: agree. Add a canary rollout: 5% hosts first, monitor kv_growth_slope and OOM_count.
oliver: telemetry note: add gauge kv_fragmentation_ratio = free_fragments_bytes / total_free_bytes. Need alert if >0.6 for >10m.
bot-deploy: deploy patch r/infra/kv/evict-throttle landed to canary pool (job 4823).
maria: thanks — I'll flip compaction now on the affected pool and watch.
jamal: after flipping, watch reclaim rate and kv_pool_used slope. Add tracing to correlate reuse pointer churn with batch sizes.
maria: initial observation after flag flip: reclaim jumped to 150MB/min, kv used slope flattened within 12m. No further host evicts in 30m.
tessa: great. Next steps: design the slab coalescer proposal doc and timeline, add the kernel+allocator guard, and add the graceful-degrade routing policy to the router.
jamal: assign owners: coalescer -> jamal, kernel guard -> tessa, routing policy -> oliver. I'll add tickets.
oliver: we'll also create a short runbook entry: on KV longctx growth detect -> flip compaction -> if >15m no improvement, evacuate long sessions and mark host for deeper forensic.
maria: thanks team. Closing loop with customer once we have the canary stable. :thumbsup:
